spirit.name: Maker's Mark
spirit.description: Smooth, approachable bourbon with caramel and vanilla sweetness, finished with gentle oak spice.
spirit.longDescription: Maker's Mark is a classic Kentucky bourbon known for its mellow, rounded character. Expect a soft sweetness up front, warming spice through the middle, and a smooth finish that makes it perfect neat, over ice, or lengthened with your favourite mixer.
servingSuggestions: Neat or over a single cube
Bourbon & cola with a fresh lime squeeze
Classic Old Fashioned with orange oils

spirit.name: Tanqueray Blackcurrant Royale
spirit.description: A rich, fruity twist on Tanqueray with bold blackcurrant and a hint of vanilla sweetness.
spirit.longDescription: Tanqueray Blackcurrant Royale brings a luxurious berry note to your gin serve. It's vibrant, smooth and brilliantly easy to enjoy as a G&T, with lemonade, or in a sparkling spritz for a fruit-forward refresher.
servingSuggestions: With tonic and a lemon wedge
With lemonade over plenty of ice
Top with Prosecco for a Royale spritz

spirit.name: Bushmills
spirit.description: Classic Irish whiskey: light, smooth and easy-drinking with gentle fruit and honey notes.
spirit.longDescription: Bushmills is a well-loved Irish whiskey with a smooth character that works brilliantly neat, on the rocks, or lengthened with ginger ale. It's an easy way to explore Irish whiskey flavours without the burn.
servingSuggestions: Neat or over ice
With ginger ale and a lime wedge
In a simple Whiskey Sour

spirit.name: Warners Elderflower Gin
spirit.description: A floral, hedgerow-fresh gin with delicate elderflower sweetness and a bright, refreshing finish.
spirit.longDescription: Warners Elderflower Gin brings a countryside lift to your glass with soft floral notes balanced by classic juniper. It's ideal for a crisp G&T, an elderflower-forward highball, or a light springtime spritz.
servingSuggestions: Elderflower tonic and a fresh lime wedge
Premium tonic with cucumber ribbon
Elderflower Collins with lemon and soda

spirit.name: Gordon's Tropical Passionfruit
spirit.description: Tropical, fruity and super refreshing — passionfruit sweetness with a light gin backbone.
spirit.longDescription: Gordon's Tropical Passionfruit is a bright, fruit-forward pour that's made for long, sunny afternoons. Enjoy it long with tonic or lemonade, and ask the bar team for a garnish that brings the tropical notes forward.
servingSuggestions: With tonic and a squeeze of lime
With lemonade over plenty of ice
Add a splash of soda for extra refreshment

education.story: This is the easy-going side of gin: still built on a gin base, but led by ripe passionfruit aroma, soft tropical sweetness and a lighter citrus finish. It is a good first step for guests who usually choose spritzes, fruit ciders or cocktails and want something long, cold and refreshing.
education.whyPicked: May is when the garden starts to feel useful again. We picked Gordon's Tropical Passionfruit because it works as a sunny, no-fuss long drink before food, after work, or with a table of friends who all want something approachable.
education.flavourProfile: Expect passionfruit first, then citrus lift, then a gentle gin dryness underneath. Compared with a classic London Dry, this drinks softer, fruitier and sweeter.
education.perfectServe: Tall glass, plenty of ice, lemonade or tonic, and a squeeze of lime. Choose lemonade for a sweeter tropical serve, or tonic if you want the gin side to show through.
foodPairings: Stone-baked pizza with chilli, pepperoni or roasted vegetables
Fish and chips, where the citrus and passionfruit cut through the batter
Salty bar snacks or chips shared in the garden
education.barTeamTip: If you are not sure whether to choose tonic or lemonade, start with lemonade. If you normally find flavoured gin too sweet, ask for tonic and extra lime.

glossary.definition: Gin with added flavour after distillation. The best examples keep the gin structure while making one fruit or botanical easy to spot.
The piney, dry botanical that makes gin taste like gin. In fruit-led gins it sits behind the main flavour.
A spirit served tall over ice with a mixer, designed to be refreshing rather than strong and short.

spirit.name: Williams Chase Pink Grapefruit Gin
spirit.description: Crisp, citrusy and fresh — bright pink grapefruit with a clean gin finish.
spirit.longDescription: Williams Chase Pink Grapefruit Gin is all about zesty, bittersweet citrus. It's brilliant with tonic and a grapefruit wedge, and it makes a cracking base for long summer serves when you want something light, fresh and flavour-packed.
servingSuggestions: With premium tonic and a grapefruit wedge
With soda and a twist of lemon
In a Grapefruit Gin Spritz with sparkling wine

education.story: Pink grapefruit gin is all about contrast: bright citrus aroma, a little natural bitterness, and enough gin dryness to keep the serve crisp. It is more grown-up than a very sweet fruit gin, but still easy to drink.
education.whyPicked: June needs something sharp, cold and clean. This bottle earns its place because grapefruit works beautifully in a pub garden serve: aromatic on the nose, refreshing with tonic, and lively enough to stand up to food.
education.flavourProfile: Zesty grapefruit peel, light bitterness, clean citrus and a dry gin finish. The key word is crisp rather than sweet.
education.perfectServe: Premium tonic, lots of ice and a wedge or twist of grapefruit. For something lighter, ask for soda and a squeeze of lemon.
foodPairings: Fish and chips, especially with extra lemon
Chicken or vegetable pizzas with fresh herbs
Sunday roast turkey, where citrus helps lift the gravy and potatoes
education.barTeamTip: Grapefruit can read sweeter or sharper depending on the mixer. Tonic keeps it dry; soda makes it lighter; lemonade makes it much fruitier.

glossary.definition: The aromatic oils in citrus peel. They give grapefruit drinks their bright smell before you even taste them.
A flavour balance where sweetness is checked by a bitter edge, common in grapefruit and aperitif-style drinks.
A lighter mixed drink usually built with bubbles, ice and a bright flavour base.

spirit.name: Captain Morgan's Tiki
spirit.description: A tropical, easy-going rum with bright fruit flavour that shines in long summer serves.
spirit.longDescription: Captain Morgan's Tiki is a fun, fruit-led rum made for holiday-vibe mixers. Keep it simple with cola and lime, or go full tropical with pineapple juice and plenty of ice.
servingSuggestions: With cola and fresh lime
With pineapple juice over ice
In a simple rum punch with citrus

education.story: Flavoured rum is built for mixing: the rum brings soft sugarcane depth and spice, while the tropical fruit character makes the drink bright and holiday-like. Captain Morgan's Tiki sits firmly in the long, fun, summer-drink camp.
education.whyPicked: July is made for relaxed serves. We chose this because it can go simple with cola, brighter with pineapple juice, or party-style as the base of a rum punch.
education.flavourProfile: Tropical fruit sweetness, soft vanilla, gentle spice and a smooth rum finish. It is rounded rather than dry.
education.perfectServe: Pineapple juice over plenty of ice, finished with a squeeze of lime. Cola and lime works well if you prefer a darker, simpler serve.
foodPairings: Burgers, especially with barbecue or chilli heat
Spicy pizza toppings
Salty chips or loaded sides shared with friends
education.barTeamTip: A squeeze of lime matters here. It reins in the sweetness and makes the tropical fruit taste fresher.

glossary.definition: Rum with added fruit, spice or other flavouring, usually designed for easy mixed drinks.
A mixed drink style that balances spirit, fruit, sweetness and citrus.
A tall drink made with spirit, mixer and ice. Rum and pineapple is a classic highball structure.

spirit.name: Jose Cuervo Silver Tequila
spirit.description: Crisp, clean tequila with fresh agave flavour — ideal for Margaritas and tequila highballs.
spirit.longDescription: Jose Cuervo Silver is a bright, clean tequila that mixes beautifully. Go classic with a Margarita, keep it refreshing with tequila, soda and lime, or ask for a simple Paloma-style serve.
servingSuggestions: Margarita with fresh lime
Tequila soda with lime
Paloma-style with grapefruit soda

education.story: Silver tequila keeps the focus on fresh agave rather than oak. That makes it bright, crisp and cocktail-friendly: exactly the style you want in a Margarita, tequila soda or grapefruit serve.
education.whyPicked: August is peak citrus-and-ice weather. Jose Cuervo Silver gives us a clean tequila special that teaches people tequila can be refreshing and food-friendly, not just a shot.
education.flavourProfile: Fresh agave sweetness, citrus lift and a clean finish. It is sharper and lighter than aged tequila styles.
education.perfectServe: A simple Margarita with lime, or a tall tequila soda with fresh lime if you want something lighter. Grapefruit soda gives a Paloma-style serve.
foodPairings: Fish and chips with extra lime or lemon
Chicken dishes and lighter pizzas
Anything with chilli, where tequila's citrus edge helps
tryIfYouLike: Vodka soda with lime, but want more character
education.barTeamTip: If tequila has only ever meant shots, try it tall with soda and lime. You taste the agave without the sweetness of a cocktail.

glossary.definition: The plant used to make tequila. It gives tequila its green, lightly sweet and peppery character.
A clear tequila style that is usually chosen for freshness and mixing rather than oak-aged richness.
A tequila and grapefruit drink style. It is bright, fizzy and less sweet than many tropical cocktails.

spirit.name: Chase Sloe Gin
spirit.description: Rich, fruity and gently warming — a classic sloe gin with berry depth and a soft almond finish.
spirit.longDescription: Chase Sloe Gin is a beautifully fruit-led pour with a smooth, rounded character. Expect hedgerow berries up front, a touch of sweetness, and a comforting finish that's brilliant neat, over ice, or lengthened with tonic.
tastingNotes: Dark berry fruit and jam notes
servingSuggestions: Neat over ice
With tonic and an orange twist
Top with Prosecco for a sparkling serve

education.story: Sloe gin is one of Britain's great hedgerow drinks: gin softened and deepened by sloe berries, giving dark fruit, gentle sweetness and a warming finish. It bridges summer drinking and autumn evenings neatly.
education.whyPicked: September sits between seasons. Chase Sloe Gin gives us something that still works with bubbles, but starts to bring richer berry notes for cooler nights.
education.flavourProfile: Dark berry fruit, jammy depth, soft almond-like sweetness and a gentle warming finish.
education.perfectServe: Neat over ice if you want the fruit to lead, with tonic for a longer drink, or topped with Prosecco for a sparkling berry serve.
foodPairings: Roast pork or turkey, where berry notes work like a fruit sauce
Cheese and savoury snacks
Desserts with apple, berry or almond flavours
education.barTeamTip: Sloe gin changes a lot with the serve. Over ice it feels rich; with tonic it becomes sharper; with bubbles it turns into a celebration drink.

glossary.definition: The small dark fruit of the blackthorn bush. It gives sloe gin its deep berry flavour.
The process of steeping fruit in alcohol so colour, aroma and flavour move into the spirit.
A drink served before food to wake up the palate. A lighter sloe gin serve can work this way.

spirit.name: Kraken Rum
spirit.description: Dark, spiced and warming — rich molasses depth with a bold, aromatic finish.
spirit.longDescription: Kraken Rum is a proper autumn pour: dark, spiced and full of character. Enjoy it with cola and lime, with ginger beer for a stormy-style serve, or simply over ice when you want something rich and warming.
servingSuggestions: With cola and a lime wedge
With ginger beer and fresh lime
Neat over ice for a slow sip

education.story: Black spiced rum is rum turned towards the darker end of the flavour wheel: molasses, vanilla, baking spice and a fuller finish. Kraken is bold enough to make a simple mixer feel like a proper drink.
education.whyPicked: October needs something with atmosphere. As the nights draw in, this is the bottle for cola, ginger beer and slow, warming serves after food.
education.flavourProfile: Dark sugar, molasses, vanilla, warming spice and a bold finish that lingers.
education.perfectServe: Ginger beer and fresh lime for a stormy-style serve, or cola and lime if you want the pub classic.
foodPairings: Beef pie or rich gravy-led dishes
Burgers with smoky or barbecue flavours
Chocolate or sticky desserts
education.barTeamTip: Ginger beer brings out the spice. Cola brings out the vanilla and dark sugar. Choose the mixer based on which side you want to taste.

glossary.definition: A dark sugar by-product often associated with rum. It brings treacle-like depth and richness.
Rum flavoured with spices such as vanilla, clove-style warmth or baking-spice notes.
A tall rum, ginger beer and lime serve. It is spicy, refreshing and darker than a cola mixer.

spirit.name: Monkey Shoulder
spirit.description: A smooth, modern whisky with mellow malt sweetness, soft spice and a rounded finish.
spirit.longDescription: Monkey Shoulder is a crowd-pleasing blended malt that's brilliant neat, over ice or in cocktails. Expect gentle vanilla sweetness, a touch of orange and spice, and a smooth finish that makes it easy to enjoy.
servingSuggestions: Neat or on the rocks
With ginger ale and orange twist
In a Whisky Sour

education.story: Blended malt Scotch is about balance: malt whisky character without the rough edges that can put new whisky drinkers off. Monkey Shoulder is smooth, rounded and built to work neat, over ice or in cocktails.
education.whyPicked: November is whisky weather, but we wanted an approachable bottle rather than something intimidating. This is a good bridge between classic Scotch and modern mixed whisky drinks.
education.flavourProfile: Honeyed malt, vanilla, soft orange, gentle spice and a smooth finish.
education.perfectServe: Neat or over ice for the classic route, ginger ale and orange for a long serve, or a Whisky Sour if you want citrus and texture.
foodPairings: Roast beef or beef pie
Cheese-led snacks and savoury boards
Puddings with vanilla, apple or caramel
education.barTeamTip: If you are whisky-curious, ask for it with ginger ale first. You still get malt and spice, but the serve stays bright and easy.

glossary.definition: A Scotch made by combining malt whiskies from more than one distillery, without grain whisky.
Barley that has been prepared for brewing or distilling. It gives whisky cereal, honey and biscuit-like notes.
A cocktail structure balancing whisky, lemon and sweetness for a sharper, lighter serve.

spirit.name: Disaronno
spirit.description: Iconic Italian amaretto — smooth almond sweetness with a hint of cherry and warming spice.
spirit.longDescription: Disaronno is a classic after-dinner favourite with a rich almond character. Enjoy it over ice, lengthened with cola, or in an Amaretto Sour for a festive cocktail that hits the spot.
servingSuggestions: Over ice as a digestif
With cola and a squeeze of lemon
In a classic Amaretto Sour

education.story: Amaretto is a liqueur built around almond-like sweetness, soft spice and a dessert-friendly finish. Disaronno is the classic name people recognise, and December is when that after-dinner style makes most sense.
education.whyPicked: December calls for something festive without being heavy. Disaronno works over ice, with cola, or as an Amaretto Sour, so it can be a quiet digestif or a proper cocktail.
education.flavourProfile: Sweet almond, marzipan, hints of cherry, soft spice and a smooth finish.
education.perfectServe: Over ice after food, with cola and lemon for a longer pub serve, or as an Amaretto Sour for a festive cocktail.
foodPairings: Chocolate desserts
Christmas pudding or mince-pie flavours
Coffee, especially after a meal
tryIfYouLike: Baileys-style after-dinner drinks but want something brighter
education.barTeamTip: If you find liqueurs too sweet, ask for an Amaretto Sour. Lemon changes the drink completely and makes the almond notes feel sharper.

glossary.definition: An Italian-style liqueur known for almond-like sweetness and a soft, dessert-friendly finish.
A sweetened spirit, often flavoured with fruit, nuts, herbs, spice or coffee.
A drink served after food. Sweet or aromatic liqueurs are often used this way.
